facts.text: InvertedPendulumPyBulletEnv-v0 is registered with entry point pybulletgym.envs.roboschool.envs.pendulum.inverted_pendulum_env:InvertedPendulumBulletEnv
The InvertedPendulumPyBulletEnv-v0 registration sets max_episode_steps to 1000
The inverted pendulum robot declares action_dim=1 and obs_dim=5
The action space is a one-element Box with both bounds from np.ones([action_dim]), that is -1 and 1
The observation space is a Box of obs_dim elements with bounds from -np.inf to np.inf
The observation vector is [cart position, cart velocity, cos(theta), sin(theta), theta angular velocity]
apply_action sets the slider motor torque to 100 times the action clipped to -1 to 1
The reset draws the pole angle uniformly from -0.1 to 0.1 (the swing-up reset adds 3.1415) and sets the motor torque to 0
The non-swing-up episode terminates when abs(theta) is greater than 0.2 and each step pays reward 1.0
The environment creates a scene with gravity 9.8, timestep 0.0165 s and frame_skip 1
The scene stores timestep and frame_skip and computes dt as timestep times frame_skip
The MJCF model gives the cart a slide joint named slider on the x axis with range -1 to 1 and the pole an unlimited hinge
The documented gym environment methods are reset(self), which returns the observation, and step(self, action), which returns observation, reward, done and info
The environments are reimplemented with the pybullet wrapper of Bullet Physics

determinism.notes: the upstream environment seeds gym.utils.seeding.np_random and shares that generator with the robot, and the fake seeds Python's random.Random with the reset seed; the two generators are different, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on both implementations

gaps: Bullet rigid-body simulation of the cart, slider joint and pole hinge: the fake integrates a simplified cart-pole model with placeholder masses and arm length, not Bullet's joints, contacts, solver or integrator, so trajectories differ
the fake draws the initial pole angle with Python's random.Random; upstream draws it from numpy's generator through gym.utils.seeding
the fake applies the registered 1000-step limit itself and returns a five-tuple; upstream step() returns a four-tuple and gym.make adds the TimeLimit wrapper
no rendering, camera adjustment or HUD is modelled
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulated world stops advancing: after an e-stop every step and reset is refused and the last observation stays readable until the runtime's safety reset clears the latch
